tickerNote: US & Europe close Tue 10 Nov · India: Mon 9 Nov (markets shut Tue for Diwali Balipratipada)

lead.headline: Hot Inflation Print Halts Wall Street's Rebound as Traders Bet on a December Fed Hike
lead.deck: October consumer prices ran ahead of forecasts, lifting the 10-year Treasury yield briefly above 5% and pulling stocks lower a day after their best session since April.
body: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against a forecast of 0.3%, after a 0.6% rise in September, and core prices excluding food and energy climbed 0.3% versus an expected 0.2%. Gasoline, shelter and food all rose. No comparable annual rate was published because the 2025 government shutdown disrupted the year-earlier data.

Futures markets moved to price a December rate increase as close to certain: CME data showed odds of roughly 99% after the release, with about an 11% chance of a half-point move. The Fed's target range sits at 3.75%–4%, and Governor Christopher Waller said a larger step could be warranted if core pressures persist.

Bonds took the first hit. The two-year Treasury yield rose about 18 basis points to near 4.73%, on course for its largest daily jump since the April 2025 tariff shock, while the 10-year briefly topped 5% before settling just below it. Gold fell about 2.6% to around $4,032 an ounce and silver dropped more than 3.5%.

Stocks gave back part of Monday's rally, when the S&P 500 rose 2.35% and the Nasdaq 2.74%. On Tuesday the S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 7,520.93, the Dow lost 157.86 points to 52,231.89 and the Nasdaq fell 0.74% to 25,065.87. Nvidia dropped another 5.5% amid a board inquiry into its chief executive. Europe mostly edged higher on cheaper oil, and Indian markets, shut on Tuesday for Diwali Balipratipada, reopen today.

top: Hotter-than-expected US inflation pushed the 10-year yield briefly above 5% and left futures pricing a December Fed hike as near-certain.
Nvidia fell about 5.5% for a second straight loss as an independent board committee examines CEO Jensen Huang's conduct.
Anthropic set a $70–$78 IPO range for up to $64.4 billion, plus a $26 billion placement with chip and cloud partners; trading on Nasdaq is slated for 19 November.
Samsung Fire & Marine agreed, with KKR and Korea's sovereign fund, to buy the rest of Lloyd's insurer Canopius in a deal reported at about $2.2 billion.
SEBI cleared MakeMyTrip's India listing, and coffee brand Blue Tokai's FY26 revenue topped ₹500 crore as Indian markets reopen after Diwali.

items.headline: October Inflation Overshoots
items.body: Headline and core consumer prices each beat forecasts by a tenth of a point. Futures now treat a December rate rise as all but certain, with some bets on a half-point move.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Jump Across the Curve
items.body: The two-year yield was on track for its biggest one-day rise since April 2025, and the 10-year briefly broke above 5% before easing just under that level.

items.headline: Europe Edges Higher on Cheaper Oil
items.body: Brent briefly slipped below $90 a barrel on hopes of easing US–Iran tensions before recovering to about $92. The DAX added 0.31% and Milan 0.69%, while London's FTSE 100 lagged at 10,751.59.

items.headline: Asia Rallied Before the Data
items.body: Seoul closed at 5,239.13 and Tokyo at 60,459.58 on Tuesday as AI-linked shares recovered from last week's rout. India was shut for Diwali Balipratipada; the rupee last settled 5 paise firmer at 93.93 to the dollar on Monday.

items.headline: Nvidia Slides for a Second Day
items.body: Outside counsel and a committee of independent directors are reviewing CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy; the board says it has no reason to think national security or company secrets were compromised. The stock briefly dipped below a $4 trillion market value, and results are due 17 November.

items.headline: Meta Rises on JPMorgan Endorsement
items.body: Meta Platforms gained more than 5% after JPMorgan added it to its Focus List, one of the few large technology names to rise on the day.

items.headline: Gold Miners and Homebuilders Hit by Yields
items.body: Mining shares fell roughly twice as much as bullion, and housing stocks retreated, with Lennar among the decliners, on worries that higher yields will push up mortgage rates.

items.headline: Lenders Led Dalal Street's Monday Gain
items.body: In India's last session the Nifty rose 58.25 points and the Sensex 107 points. State Bank of India, Trent and Nestlé India led, pharma stocks gained 1.65%, and IT shares fell 1.22%.

items.headline: Berlin Buys Into Tank Maker KNDS
items.body: Germany agreed last week to pay €6.6 billion for the founding families' half of the Leopard 2 maker, based on an €11.2 billion valuation plus a €1 billion premium. Berlin and Paris aim to trim their holdings to 40% each in a future IPO.

items.headline: EP Group Takes Control of Fnac Darty
items.body: Daniel Křetínský's EP Group now holds 69.3% of the French electronics retailer after its tender offer closed on 9 November; under French rules the offer reopens for further tenders.

items.headline: Samsung Fire Moves to Control Canopius
items.body: Samsung Fire & Marine, together with funds managed by KKR and Korea Investment Corporation, will buy the Centerbridge-led consortium's stake. Samsung's holding will rise to 80.6%, with KKR taking 12.1% and KIC 7.3%.

items.headline: Argenx and Huaxin Strike Deals
items.body: Argenx will pay $550 million upfront, plus up to $595 million in milestones, for oral-peptide specialist Unnatural Products, and China's Huaxin agreed to buy Brazilian steelmaker CSN's cement arm at a $2.31 billion enterprise value.

items.headline: October Losses Spread Across Big Names
items.body: Macro manager Rokos (about $22bn) fell in October but remains up roughly 8% for the year, while Viking's cautious AI stance limited its loss. Lone Pine lost 9% and Tiger Global 8.5%.

items.headline: Stock Pickers Nurse a Historic Rout
items.body: Goldman Sachs data showed fundamental and systematic long/short funds both lost more than 3% in October, a first in its records, and cut net leverage at the fastest pace since March. Walleye, Engineers Gate and Brevan Howard have shed staff.

items.headline: Multistrategy Giants Split
items.body: Citadel's Wellington fund gained in October and is up 15.3% this year, and D.E. Shaw's Composite added 0.7%. Millennium lost ground and is withdrawing more than $1.5 billion from external managers Troluce and Axebrook.

items.headline: Bridgewater's Co-CIO Heads to Ottawa
items.body: Karen Karniol-Tambour will leave Bridgewater after about two decades to become the first chief executive of the Canada Strong Fund, the country's new sovereign wealth fund.

items.headline: Anthropic Sets Its IPO Range
items.body: After pulling an earlier draft over pricing errors, the AI company filed terms for 825 million shares on Nasdaq under 'ANT', plus a private placement with AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. CNBC puts the fully diluted value at up to about $1.4 trillion, with pricing expected 18 November.

items.headline: Barrick Files to List North American Arm
items.body: Barrick Mining filed with the SEC to float a minority stake, earlier flagged at about 10%, in American Barrick Gold, which will hold its Nevada Gold Mines and Pueblo Viejo interests and the Fourmile project.

items.headline: MakeMyTrip Cleared; ShareChat's Loss Widens
items.body: SEBI cleared MakeMyTrip's Indian arm to list through a pure offer for sale by its Nasdaq-listed parent. Separately, ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech's FY26 consolidated loss rose about 79% as revenue grew 40% to ₹1,016 Cr, swollen by share-based pay and currency losses.

items.fig: Blue Tokai rev ₹518 Cr · D2C 36 of 108 deals
items.headline: Consumer Brands Draw Capital and Scale
items.body: Coffee brand Blue Tokai's FY26 revenue rose about 59% while its loss widened to ₹83 Cr. D2C startups took a third of Indian funding deals in October, and jewellery brand GIVA's roughly $100 million round led a busy first week of November.
